content:
The existence of a tent in the post-war era played a major role in reducing the casualties due to lack of medical care. Rufaidah daughter of Sa’ad al-Anshari (Rufaidah Al-Aslamia) is listed as the owner of a first-rate treatment tent in Islamic history.

Rufaidah is a descendant of Bani Aslam who helped welcome the arrival and Islam of the Prophet Muhammad in Medina.

He adhered to the Messenger of Allah after the migration. It participated in two wars, the Khandaq War and the Khaibar War.

His interest in the world of medicine has been started since childhood. His father, Saad al-Aslami, was a physiotherapist.

Rufaidah learned from observing her father’s activities and grew up to become an expert in medicine.

Rufaidah was indeed not given full responsibility like men who could carry out operations and amputations.

However, he was instrumental in treating and providing motivation to the Islamic mujahid. He was nicknamed Fidaiyah for entering the battlefield to bring the wounded.

Rufaidah’s care tent first appeared during the Battle of Uhud. At that time, Rufaidah went out in battle and brought all the equipment, including the tent he needed on the camel. He pitched his tent before the Muslim soldiers. The sahabiyah helped him.

This tent was later called Rufaidah al-Aslamiah. It was the first field-care tent in the Islamic struggle. In the tent, he treated the fighters’ wounds and kept them up at night.
